translationRepairs: After Zhiyou capitulated, Qing absorbed his troops under the banner of the Qisheng Battalion and was promoted by recommendation to the rank of battalion commander.
After Zhiyou capitulated, Qing absorbed his troops under the banner of the Qisheng Battalion and was promoted by recommendation to the rank of qianzong (company officer).
薦授千總 names the Green Standard company-grade office qianzong; 'battalion commander' over-ranks the title, and the proposed gloss is accurate.
When Zhiyou surrendered, [Qing] thereupon took over command of his forces, styled the camp Qisheng, and was recommended and appointed a battalion commander.
When Zhiyou surrendered, [Qing] thereupon took over command of his forces, styled the camp Qisheng, and was recommended and appointed a qianzong (company officer).
Literal likewise misrenders 千總 as battalion commander; qianzong (company officer) matches the Qing grade.
He was granted the second-class Order of the Chariot of War and appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.
He was granted the second-class Light Chariot Commandant (qingche duwei) and appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.
予二等輕車都尉 is a Qing hereditary noble rank, not an Order of the Chariot of War; Light Chariot Commandant is the correct title.
He was granted the second-class Order of the Chariot of War and appointed Provincial Military Commander of Hunan.
He was granted the second-class Light Chariot Commandant (qingche duwei) and appointed Provincial Military Commander of Hunan.
Literal repeats the same 輕車都尉 error; second-class Light Chariot Commandant restores the hereditary rank.
Qing was roughly the same age and rank as the other generals; suddenly placed over them, many resented his command, and the seventy-odd camps of allied forces fell into disorder.
Qing was roughly the same age and seniority as the other generals; suddenly placed over them, many resented his command, and the seventy-odd camps of allied forces fell into disorder.
行輩相若 marks shared generational/peer seniority, not official 品級 rank; replacing 'rank' with 'seniority' corrects the sense.
When the Japanese crossed the Yalu, the Chinese were defeated and fell back toward Fengcheng, then made their stand on Dagao Ridge.
When the Japanese crossed the Yalu, the Chinese were defeated; the enemy pressed straight toward Fengcheng, and the Chinese fell back to hold Dagao Ridge.
直趨鳳凰城 is the Japanese drive on Fengcheng after 戰失利; 退扼大高嶺 is the Qing fallback. The proposed agent split matches the Chinese.
When eastern affairs began, Qing as Lüshun defender went to guard Jiuliancheng; Hongzhang separately ordered Jiang Guaiti and others to defend Lüshun, with Bangdao assisting.
When eastern affairs began, Qing as Lüshun defender went to guard Jiuliancheng; Li Hongzhang separately ordered Jiang Guaiti and others to defend Lüshun, with Bangdao assisting.
Chinese names 李鴻章 in full; bare 'Hongzhang' drops the surname and leaves the agent ambiguous, while Li Hongzhang restores it.
He entered service as a military student under Song Qing in campaigns against the Nian rebels, rose through merit to colonel, and received the Manchu honorific Zhenyong Batulu.
He entered service as a military student under Song Qing in campaigns against the Nian rebels, rose through merit to major, and received the Manchu honorific Zhenyong Batulu.
積功至都司 is the Qing grade dusí, conventionally major and below 參將; 'colonel' conflates distinct ranks.
As a military student he followed Song Qing against the Nian, accumulated merit to colonel, and was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
As a military student he followed Song Qing against the Nian, accumulated merit to major, and was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
Literal likewise over-ranks 都司 as colonel; major is the required Green Standard equivalent.

Before long the Japanese massed in great numbers; Qing fell into heavy encirclement, fell from his horse wounded, Yukun broke through the encirclement to enter, escorted him out on both sides, and casualties were exceptionally heavy.

Before long the Japanese massed in great numbers; Qing fell into heavy encirclement, fell from his horse wounded; Yukun broke through the encirclement to enter, shielded him and brought him out, and casualties were exceptionally heavy.
翼之出 uses 翼 as a verb 'to shield/flank and bring out'; 'escorted him out on both sides' misreads 翼 as a noun of sides.

At that time the Russians, because of disputes over revising the Ili treaty, had words of breach; the Uliastai consultant Xichang had long known I Ketang'a was versed in tactics and requested an edict to recruit hunters nearby to guard Hunchun.

At that time the Russians, over revision of the Ili treaty, raised objections; the Uliastai consultant Xichang had long known I Ketang'a was versed in tactics and requested an edict to recruit hunters nearby to guard Hunchun.
有違言 means there were objections or discordant words over revising the Ili treaty; 'had words of breach' is an inaccurate calque.
In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was given the posthumous name Chengyong, Loyal and Brave, and a memorial temple.
In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was given the posthumous name Chengyong and a memorial temple was granted.
諡誠勇，予建祠 bestows only the posthumous name Chengyong and a temple grant; 'Loyal and Brave' is an inserted gloss treated as part of the name.
Once he arrived, they deliberated to use attack as defense.
Once they arrived, they deliberated to use attack as defense.
既至 follows the joint charge of Zhang Shun and I Ketang'a; singular 'he' conflicts with that plural arrival, and 'they' matches 議.
After the war his Yu Battalion grew insubordinate; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and Rong He was stripped of rank and punished.
After the war his Yu Battalion grew insubordinate; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and Rong He was stripped of office and punished.
革職治罪 is removal from office and punishment; 'stripped of rank' overstates 革職, while 'stripped of office' is exact.
When the Xiang Army general Chen Ti arrived he again asked Liu Kunyi for a combined assault — again without result.
When the Xiang Army general Chen Shi arrived he again asked Liu Kunyi for a combined assault — again without result.
陳湜 reads Chen Shi (湜 = shí); 'Chen Ti' is a wrong character reading, and the proposed spelling matches the Chinese.
When the Hunan Army general Chen Ti arrived, he again asked Liu Kunyi to order a joint attack — again without success.
When the Hunan Army general Chen Shi arrived, he again asked Liu Kunyi to order a joint attack — again without success.
Literal likewise misspells 陳湜 as Chen Ti; Chen Shi is the correct reading.
Song Qing and Yukun suffered defeats in succession and could no longer recover their strength.
Song Qing and Ma Yukun suffered defeats in succession and could no longer recover their strength.
慶與玉昆 pairs Song Qing with Ma Yukun; once Qing is expanded to Song Qing, bare Yukun should carry the surname Ma already used in the idiomatic line.
